title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority routing, burst controls, and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Ethan Li
release_notes: Enhances dedicated autoscaler with priority routing for burst traffic, improved token-bucket smoothing, and additional utilization metrics for fleet-level dashboards. Backwards compatible; no breaking changes.
description: Context: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while supporting short-lived burst traffic from high-priority customers. Motivation: customers using Dedicated capacity have requested (1) per-priority burst controls so high-tier customers retain latency guarantees during spikes and (2) richer utilization reporting per-priority to drive capacity planning. This PR implements priority-aware routing in the autoscaler, integrates token-bucket smoothing per-priority, and emits new utilization metrics for the fleet dashboards. Changes include: priority router that prefers reserved capacity for higher priorities, fallback to shared burst pool with configurable throttle thresholds; per-priority token-bucket smoothing to avoid oscillation during rapid load changes; new Prometheus metrics (fleet_capacity_{priority}, burst_tokens_{priority}, utilization_5m_{priority}); dashboard panels and alert updates. Testing: unit tests for routing and smoothing, integration test exercising priority fallback behavior, small canary perf run on staging. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-8791) - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration test added - [x] dashboard updates - [x] e2e canary run (staging) - [x] changelog/release notes. Notes: defaults preserve current behavior for clusters that do not opt into priority routing; config is behind feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.priority_routing. See linked Linear ticket ENG-8791 for rollout plan and SLAs.

conversation: Priya Natarajan (reviewer): Overall looks solid. A few suggestions: make the token-bucket defaults conservative, and add a comment on how the smoothing window maps to the rolling metrics. Also please add a graceful degradation test where metric emission fails.

Ethan Li (author): Thanks Priya — adjusted defaults to max_burst_tokens=200 and smoothing_window_ms=5000. Added tests for metric exporter failure in tokenbucket_smoother_test.go and a note in the design doc.
Daniel Park (reviewer): Left inline comment on priority routing behavior when multiple high-priority requests exceed reserved capacity. Can we ensure deterministic tie-breaker to avoid flapping?
Ethan Li (author): Added deterministic tie-breaker (by request timestamp then request id) and unit tests to prove stability under equal weights.
Marisol Gomez (approver): Verified canary perf numbers on staging (p95 tail preserved for priority traffic, overall fleet utilization within expected bounds). Approving to merge once CI green.
ci_checks: e2e-dedicated-canary: pass (staging run: 10k reqs, p95 latency delta <5%)
merge_details: Merged by Marisol Gomez using squash merge. Squash commit: 'feat(autoscaler): priority routing, burst controls, and utilization metrics (ENG-8791)'. Rollout: feature flag disabled by default; ops will enable per-cluster with gradual ramp described in ENG-8791.
notes: Rollout plan: enable in staging -> monitor utilization and p95 for high-priority customers -> enable in tiered production clusters behind feature flag. Dashboard and alerts added; recommend watch window of 48 hours during initial enablement.
test_instructions: To exercise locally: make sure helm values.yaml sets dedicated.autoscaler.priority_routing=true and run 'make canary-perf' which runs the staging_canary script and integration tests. Use examples/dedicated/priority-config.example.yaml for config knobs.
